content: h1. INC: Usage page delayed for Batch API jobs
Status: resolved.
h1. Window
2027-03-15 02:00 UTC to 2027-03-15 11:40 UTC.
h1. Impact
Usage for Batch API jobs that finished in the window appeared on the Console usage page up to 8 hours late. Hosted API and Embeddings usage was not affected.
h1. Resolution
The batch usage writer was restarted and all delayed batch usage was backfilled by 13:00 UTC. body: ## Scope
This applies only to the Embeddings Batch endpoint (`/v1/embeddings/batch`). Its usage is written when the whole batch finishes, so it can take up to 4 hours to appear on the Console usage page. It does not apply to Hosted API requests or ordinary embeddings calls; for those, the threshold is on the billing case routing page.
## What to tell the customer
Batch usage appears when the batch finishes. No case is needed within 4 hours of the batch finishing.
_Last reviewed 2027-03-12._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/onboarding-escalation-and-triage-playbook.json", "chunk": "20/21", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Onboarding Checklist: Support Escalation and Triage Playbook", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-08", "text": "## Appendix B: Support macros (copy/paste)

### Macro: Usage dashboard freshness
“Usage can take a short time to appear in the dashboard depending on ingestion. Please confirm you’re viewing the correct workspace and time range. If it’s been >30 minutes since your last successful requests and usage still shows 0, we’ll investigate telemetry freshness.”"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-18", "text": "## Common customer symptoms
- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.
- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.
## Recommended mitigations
1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.
2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).
3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.
4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/workaround-streaming-timeouts-and-reconnect.json", "chunk": "3/15", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Workaround: Streaming timeouts, disconnects, and reconnect guidance", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-16", "text": "(continued) ## Symptoms (what customers report)
- Customer retries can inflate apparent usage/throughput and complicate root-cause
---
## Likely causes (most common first)
| Category | What it looks like | Notes / confirmation |
|---|---|---|
| Client/proxy idle timeout | Stream stops after a fixed duration (e.g., 30s/60s/120s) especially when tokens slow down | Ask whether customer uses a CDN, API gateway, corporate proxy, ALB/NGINX, or service mesh. These commonly enforce idle read timeouts. |
| Client read timeout too low | Errors after a consistent “no data received” window | Common after SDK/client upgrades where defaults changed. |
| HTTP/2 intermediaries | More frequent resets with HTTP/2 enabled; HTTP/1.1 more stable | Some proxies/load balancers have imperfect long-lived HTTP/2 stream handling. |
| Local NAT / firewall state | Disconnects near fixed durations; more common from specific VPCs/corp networks | Often mitigated via TCP keepalive settings. |"}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-18544-usage-dashboard-lag-confusing-onboarding.json", "chunk": "5/8", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-18544: Usage dashboard appears not to count requests during onboarding (delayed usage aggregation) - customer believes API calls not being metered", "status": "Resolved", "date": "2025-03-14", "text": "  - 2025-03-12 10:15 (Nadia Rahman, Telemetry/Metering) — Looking. We had a minor delay on the usage aggregation job (partition backlog) starting ~08:50 UTC due to an upstream warehouse throttling event. Job caught up by ~10:05 UTC. Data should be visible now or within next refresh. No loss expected. Will confirm with table partition timestamps.
  - 2025-03-12 10:27 (Priya Shah, Support) — Updated customer: we identified a delay in the usage aggregation pipeline affecting the Usage dashboard; requests are still processed and will appear shortly. Asked them to refresh after ~15 minutes and confirm whether the numbers update. Reassured that metering is not lost; it’s a display/aggregation lag.
  - 2025-03-12 10:44 (BluePeak AI, Customer) — Confirmed. Usage just updated and now shows tokens/requests. Thanks. Is this going to happen regularly? We were worried because it looked like nothing was being tracked."}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-18544-usage-dashboard-lag-confusing-onboarding.json", "chunk": "2/8", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-18544: Usage dashboard appears not to count requests during onboarding (delayed usage aggregation) - customer believes API calls not being metered", "status": "Resolved", "date": "2025-03-14", "text": "- Customer concern: “requests aren’t being counted” / “metering is broken” / may impact billing and quota behavior.
Customer impact
- Confusion during onboarding; customer delayed proceeding to production test because they believed calls were not registering.
- Risk: churn / low confidence in billing accuracy.
Customer report (verbatim excerpt)
- “We can see 200 responses from the API, but the console still shows 0 requests and 0 tokens. Is our account not tracking usage?”
Environment
- Hosted API (self-serve)
- Region: us-east
- Console: Usage tab + Project overview widgets
What we checked / hypothesis
- Hypothesis A: expected aggregation delay (usage dashboard ETL ~5–20 min, sometimes longer during backfill/partition catch-up).
- Hypothesis B: requests not attributed to the correct project (wrong API key / env var) -> common onboarding failure.
- Hypothesis C: telemetry freshness issue for us-east pipeline (delayed ingestion/transform), dashboard not showing latest partition.

description: Issue summary:
Customer reported a large unexplained increase in billed token usage visible in the Console's per-tenant usage breakdown for the last 24 hours. The Console's 'unique_client_ids' metric spiked ~6x overnight. Investigation found many ingestion records with null or empty request_id fields which the analytics join logic treated as distinct clients, inflating unique counts and rolling up to billing totals.
Impact:"}]}

### Streaming cancellation
- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).
- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json", "chunk": "15/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API Packages: Free Tier, Included Usage, and Overage Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-26", "text": "### Example 3: Streaming disconnect

Some customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.
This page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/enterprise-ratelimit-quota-adjustment-and-cost-protection-playbook-2026.json", "chunk": "3/10", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Enterprise Rate Limit & Quota Adjustment — Operational Playbook", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-14", "text": "| Billing Anomaly Feed | Real-time billing spikes > configured thresholds | Finance Ops |
SLOs and Thresholds Table
-------------------------
| Signal | Warning Threshold | Critical Threshold | Initial Action |
| Tokens/min usage | 75% of quota | 90% of quota OR sudden rise > 3x baseline | Notify CS + generate invoice hold? |
| 429 error rate | 1% over 5m | 5% over 5m | Start triage, apply temporary throttles |
| Concurrent connections | 70% of allowed | 95% of allowed | Autoscale/migrate to dedicated pool |
Immediate Triage Steps (0–15 minutes)
-------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge: CS on-call acknowledges ticket/alert in Slack #cs-oncall and sets incident status.
2. Identify customer and tier: confirm customer_id, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), active models and pinned versions.
3. Gather telemetry: attach links to the customer quota dashboard, recent API logs (last 30 minutes), and billing spike report.
4. Assign Mitigation Owner: CS engineer if customer-facing actions required; escalate to SRE if platform-wide.
